claim: Workspace.FilteringEnabled is discontinued and no longer takes effect; client->server replication filtering is always on.
evidence: Quote: 'This property is discontinued and no longer takes effect.'
counterevidence: Exact year FE became mandatory (commonly 2018) not verified from official source this session.
defensive_implication: Client-made changes never reach the server; only remotes/physics-ownership/client-triggered instances cross the boundary - audit those.

claim: Instances must be created on the server to replicate; client-created instances passed via remotes arrive as nil.
evidence: Quotes: 'for an instance to replicate ... it must be created on the server'; remote.md: 'the server will see nil because the part isn't replicable'.
defensive_implication: A pet spawned in a client's DataModel is purely visual (E); inventory UI must render from server-replicated state only.

claim: Server receives sender Player as first remote argument; all other arguments are attacker-controlled (any frequency, arbitrary values, tables spoofing Instances).
evidence: Quote: 'Fire or invoke RemoteEvents and RemoteFunctions at any frequency with arbitrary arguments (besides the first Player argument)'; boundary page shows table-spoofing an Instance.
defensive_implication: Key all inventory ops by the implicit Player; validate typeof/class/IsDescendantOf for any instance argument; never accept item definitions/prices from client.

claim: Official docs show NaN bypassing range/balance checks in a trade-offer handler and propagating to other players.
evidence: Quote: 'The exploiter successfully created a trade offer without having any gold ... even spread to other players through the offer.' Recommends math.isfinite().
defensive_implication: Reject non-finite and non-integer quantities at every remote; use integer pet IDs/counts; assert invariants before commit.

claim: Official docs describe trade + leave + failed save as a duplication vector and recommend transaction-like validate-then-commit with full revert.
evidence: Quote: 'If the trade completes but their DataStore save fails ... they rejoin with their original items while the other player keeps the traded items - resulting in duplication.'
defensive_implication: Trades must be committed as one durable record applied idempotently to both inventories, with session locks; never complete a trade whose persistence is unconfirmed.

claim: Official rate-limiting guidance: never rely on client rate limits; reference server token-bucket implementation provided. No platform-enforced per-remote limit is documented.
evidence: Quote: 'never rely solely on a client-sided rate limit' + TokenBucket module.
counterevidence: Absence of platform remote limit inferred from docs; not explicitly stated.
defensive_implication: Per-player token buckets on every economy remote (trade request, accept, hatch, buy); log throttle hits as abuse signal.

claim: ProximityPrompt/ClickDetector/DragDetector events can be fired by exploiters at any distance even when disabled; only ProximityPrompt.Triggered has a server distance check.
evidence: Quotes: 'An exploiter can fire any event even if Enabled is false'; ClickDetector 'There are no checks at all on the server'.
defensive_implication: Pet shops/egg stands driven by prompts need server-side distance, state and rate checks.

claim: Clients get network ownership of nearby unanchored parts and can teleport them, spoof Touched, and replicate NaN/Inf CFrames.
evidence: Quotes: 'By default, the server grants network ownership of unanchored parts to clients'; 'Manipulate the firing of Touched events'.
defensive_implication: Never grant pets/currency from Touched on unanchored parts; anchor or SetNetworkOwner(nil) for pickups.

claim: Server authority model (Workspace.AuthorityMode=Server, client prediction + rollback) exists but is still labeled beta.
evidence: Quote: 'Server authority is currently in beta and will be released soon.'
defensive_implication: Helps movement/physics only; does not secure inventory or trade logic.

claim: Any replicated LocalScript/ModuleScript can be decompiled and any replicated content data-mined; clients can teleport to any subplace unless 'Secure within universe only' is enabled.
evidence: Quotes: 'can be decompiled by an exploiter once replicated'; 'restricts all non-start places to server-initiated teleports only'.
defensive_implication: Keep drop tables/odds logic/trade validation in ServerScriptService; leaks of unreleased pets are expected if shipped to clients early.

claim: ProcessReceipt has no time-based retry and no timeout; NotProcessedYet receipts are re-invoked only on another purchase or rejoin of any server in the experience.
evidence: Quote: 'ProcessReceipt has no time-based retry mechanism ... only called again ... if: The user successfully initiates another developer product purchase. The user re-joins any server'.
defensive_implication: Receipt handler must be correct on first delivery and safe on redelivery; pending receipts surface on join, so wait for session-locked data load.

claim: The same ProcessReceipt purchase can run on two servers concurrently, and a PurchaseGranted return may fail to record so the receipt is redelivered.
evidence: Quotes: 'might run on two different servers at the same time'; 'might still fail to be recorded on the backend, even if it returns ... PurchaseGranted'.
defensive_implication: Persist PurchaseId in the same atomic write as the grant (session lock); dedupe on PurchaseId forever, not just per session.

claim: Unresolved developer product purchases are not removed or refunded after escrow; without a ProcessReceipt callback receipts are auto-acknowledged.
evidence: Quotes: 'not removed or refunded after the escrow period expires'; 'If you don't implement a ProcessReceipt callback, your receipts will be auto-acknowledged.'
counterevidence: Contradicts older community belief in auto-refund of unresolved receipts.
defensive_implication: Monitor long-unresolved receipts as an ops alert; never leave product handlers unbound after refactors.

claim: receiptInfo includes PurchaseId (unique), PlayerId, ProductId, PlaceIdWherePurchased, CurrencySpent, CurrencyType, and ProductPurchaseChannel (InExperience/ExperienceDetailsPage/AdReward/CommerceProduct).
evidence: Quoted field list; enum ProductPurchaseChannel.
defensive_implication: Log channel + PurchaseId into an append-only purchase ledger; out-of-game Store purchases arrive on next join.

claim: MarketplaceService:BindReceiptHandler exists: per-ReceiptType (DeveloperProduct, RobuxTransferSender/Receiver) handlers returning Enum.ReceiptDecision; takes precedence and falls through to ProcessReceipt.
evidence: Quote: 'a newer alternative that processes developer product receipts (and Robux transfer receipts) through one or more bound handlers'; 'falls through to ProcessReceipt'.
counterevidence: Launch announcement date not verified (DevForum blocked).
defensive_implication: Same idempotency rules apply; duplicate registration throws - fail closed at startup.

claim: PromptRobuxTransferAsync lets Roblox Plus subscribers send 10-500 Robux to another user in-game via Roblox UI; game earns 10%; receipts to both sides may wait on parental approval.
evidence: Quotes: 'let Roblox Plus subscribers send Robux directly to other users'; 'amount must be between 10 and 500'; 'your game earns 10%'.
defensive_implication: A pet-for-Robux trade rail now exists; if used, escrow items keyed by TransferRequestId and release only on receipts; consider paid-item-trading policy and scam risk.

claim: Cross-game pass and developer product sales disabled starting May 30, 2026; Robux transfers recommended instead.
evidence: Quote: 'Starting May 30, 2026, cross-game pass sales will be disabled.'
defensive_implication: Do not design donation/trade flows around selling another game's passes.

claim: UserOwnsGamePassAsync results are cached; out-of-experience purchases may take several minutes to propagate; first entry after purchase always returns true.
evidence: Quote: 'this process might take several minutes to propagate'.
defensive_implication: Check passes server-side; re-check on PromptGamePassPurchaseFinished and on join; don't treat a false as permanent within a session.

claim: PromptProductPurchaseFinished does not mean a purchase succeeded and must not be used to grant.
evidence: Quote: 'The firing of this event does not mean that a user has successfully purchased an item.'
defensive_implication: Grant only from receipt handlers; client 'purchase succeeded' UI is non-authoritative.

claim: Transaction Refunded webhook covers dev products, passes, private servers, paid access (not subscriptions); passes/avatar items refunded by CS are auto-revoked but dev-product benefits must be removed by the developer.
evidence: Quote: 'For developer products, the benefit exists only in your experience's code, so you need to use this notification to remove the granted benefit'.
defensive_implication: Build a clawback policy for refunded currency/pets including already-traded descendants; verify roblox-signature HMAC and timestamp window; dedupe by transaction ID.

claim: Webhooks are signed with HMAC-SHA256 over timestamp.body when a secret is set; retries 5 times; replay window check recommended.
evidence: Quotes: 'roblox-signature', 'retries ... 5 times', '10-minute window is usually a good reasonable time limit'.
defensive_implication: Always configure a secret; reject unsigned/old webhooks; make refund processing idempotent.

claim: UpdateAsync re-runs the non-yielding transform until the write succeeds without a concurrent update, or the transform returns nil (per-key optimistic concurrency).
evidence: Quote: 'will call the function again, discarding the result of the previous call ... until the data is saved or until the callback function returns nil'; 'cannot yield'.
defensive_implication: Transforms must be pure and side-effect-free (no granting inside); return GetUserIds/GetMetadata to avoid clearing them.

claim: No cross-key atomic transaction API exists for DataStores; BatchGetAsync is read-only and OrderedDataStore-only.
evidence: Grep of DataStore/GlobalDataStore/MemoryStore references and data-store guides found no transaction API; BatchGetAsync quote: 'currently only supported on OrderedDataStore'.
counterevidence: Absence-of-evidence; Open Cloud reference also checked by grep only.
defensive_implication: Two-player trades need an escrow/trade-record key + idempotent apply on each side, or same-server session-locked in-memory swap followed by saves with recovery.

claim: DataStore limits: 4,194,304 chars/key; 50-char names; per-key 25 MB/min read, 4 MB/min write; experience writes 300+20xCCU/min; game servers and Open Cloud share budget; storage 500 MB + 1 MB x lifetime users.
evidence: Quoted tables.
counterevidence: Numbers stated as subject to change.
defensive_implication: Cap inventory size and string fields server-side; external tooling must self-rate-limit to avoid starving live saves.

claim: GetAsync uses a local 4-second cache by default; UseCache=false bypasses it for verification reads.
evidence: Quote: 'in a local cache for four seconds'; 'For immediate verification reads after a write, use GetAsync() with DataStoreGetOptions.UseCache = false'.
defensive_implication: Never base trade/ownership decisions on GetAsync; use UpdateAsync or uncached reads.

claim: DataStore versions: first write per key per UTC hour is kept; later writes in that hour overwrite; old versions expire 30 days after supersession.
evidence: Quote: 'Successive writes to a key in the same UTC hour permanently overwrite the previous data.'
defensive_implication: Built-in versioning is not an audit log; keep a separate append-only trade/grant ledger for investigations and rollbacks.

claim: Official player-data guide: session locking via LockId in key metadata written atomically in UpdateAsync; without it, multi-server loads cause data loss and item duplication, especially in trading games.
evidence: Quote: 'This can be particularly impactful in games that allow players to trade and is a common source of item duplication exploits.'
counterevidence: Sample code 'has not proven itself over a long period of time in a popular game'.
defensive_implication: Mandatory session locks with expiry/refresh; refuse trades until both players' data is lock-loaded; mark failed loads 'errored' and never save them.

claim: Official receipt recipe: check PurchaseId, award in memory, record PurchaseId, save; return PurchaseGranted only after save succeeds, else NotProcessedYet.
evidence: Quoted 4-step list; warning that a failed save gives the purchase free for the session.
defensive_implication: Adopt as baseline; for tradeable pets, prevent trading a just-purchased pet until its grant is durably saved.

claim: MemoryStores are non-durable (TTL max 45 days, quota 64 KB + 1.2 KB x users); hash map UpdateAsync is compare-and-retry; queues are at-least-once via invisibility timeout.
evidence: Quotes: 'don't need to be durable'; queue items 'become visible for processing again'.
defensive_implication: OK for trade locks/mailboxes with idempotent consumers; never the system of record for pets.

claim: MessagingService delivery is best effort and not guaranteed; 1 kB message limit.
evidence: Quote: 'Delivery is best effort and not guaranteed.'
defensive_implication: Cross-server gifts/trades must be persisted (DataStore) and messages used only as wake-up hints.

claim: Open Cloud API keys inherit the owner's permissions; experience restriction optional; IP allowlist and expiry optional; keys auto-expire after 60 days unused; dedicated alt account recommended for group automation.
evidence: Quotes: 'An API key's access is determined by the permissions of the user who owns it'; '60 days ... automatically expires'.
defensive_implication: Treat data-store-write keys as mint authority: least scope, per-experience restriction, IP allowlist, rotation, audit all out-of-band writes.

claim: InsertService:LoadAsset only loads assets created/owned by the game creator, shared by the owner, or owned by Roblox (plus OpenUse avatar clothing/accessories).
evidence: Quote: 'The asset must be created or owned by the game creator. The asset must be shared by the asset owner. The asset must be owned by Roblox.'
defensive_implication: A third party's uploaded mesh cannot appear as an inventory pet in your game unless your code loads it; inventory is your DataStore data (F/E outcomes only).

defensive_implication: Keep third-party loading off; never load asset IDs supplied by clients.
